standard_prerequisites.name: The subbasis theorem for quasi-compactness, through coverings by members of a subbasis
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source line 2674)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces quasi-compactness of the product to finite refinability of coverings by subbasis members.

core_obligations: Choose the subbasis: take the standard subbasis of the product consisting of the preimages of open subsets in a single factor (proof lines 2667-2673)
Reduce to a covering by subbasis members: by the subbasis theorem it suffices to show that every such covering admits a finite refinement (proof lines 2674-2678)

Analyse the covering: group the covering by the factor it comes from; if for some factor the corresponding open subsets cover that factor, quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover, and otherwise a choice of points outside the relevant unions produces a point of the product outside the covering, a contradiction (proof lines 2679-2683)
proof_roadmap: 取乘积拓扑的标准子基 B = { U_i × ∏_{i'≠i} X_{i'} }。
由子基定理，只需证任意由 B 中元素组成的覆盖有有限细化。
把覆盖按因子分组：若某因子上的那些 U_j 覆盖 X_i，由准紧取有限子覆盖即得；否则在每个因子上取不在相应并中的点，得乘积中的点不在覆盖里，矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is Tychonov's theorem in the form that a product of quasi-compact spaces is quasi-compact (author theorem at source lines 2662-2665, label theorem-tychonov); the author's own proof at source lines 2667-2684 follows it immediately and is its proof. The proof applies the subbasis theorem to the standard subbasis of the product, groups a covering by the factor it comes from and argues that either one factor is covered, giving a finite subcover, or a point of the product lies outside the covering (proof lines 2667-2683). The dichotomy on the factors is the content. H3.
